intro: The Laurel-Sky Gate opens. Excellence requires witness — what is unwitnessed does not exist here. Fight where you can be seen or fight nothing at all.
First Hollow contact through corrupted trial remnants. They were once Olympic athletes who failed their trials. Now they are Hollow husks of excellence — all form, no glory.
The trial reactivates. Every action is measured against the standard of the divine. Fall short and the trial turns against you.
The first threshold. The Laurel-Sky Gate does not test strength — it tests whether your excellence is worth remembering. Be memorable.
enemy: Corrupted trial remnants. They were athletes once — divine competitors who failed their trials. They fight with the form of excellence but none of the glory.
Hollow laurel-wraiths. They wear corrupted laurels — the wreaths of those who won and then forgot why. They fight with the bitterness of the forgotten.
Trial-constructs enforcing the old standard. They measure every action. Anything below divine excellence is punished. They are the Gate's gymnasium — and its execution chamber.
The First Trial-Master. A corrupted version of the original Olympian judge. It measures with a broken standard — one that can never be met.
mid: Fight where the trial can see you. Unwitnessed excellence does not exist here. The Gate has made visibility the condition of reality.
The laurel-wraiths are bitter. Their bitterness is their power — do not give them reason to hate. Fight with glory, not cruelty.
The trial-constructs measure everything. Be excellent — but also be creative. The old standard rewards what has been seen before. Invent a new excellence.
The First Trial-Master measures with a broken standard. You cannot meet it — it is designed to fail. Do not try to meet it. Exceed it so far it breaks.
victory: The trial recognizes your excellence. The standard was met — and the Gate recorded it. Every subsequent trial will be harder because you passed this one.
The laurel-wraiths fall. Your glory was too bright for their bitterness. The first threshold is witnessed and recorded.
The trial-constructs are satisfied — your excellence was creative enough to exceed the old standard. The Gate has a new benchmark now.
The First Trial-Master's broken standard shatters. You exceeded it so far that it could not measure you. The Laurel-Sky Gate's first threshold is yours.
defeat: Withdraw. Your excellence was unwitnessed. Return with an audience — or fight where the trial can see.
The laurel-wraiths' bitterness overwhelmed your glory. Return with brighter excellence.
The trial-constructs found you below standard. Return with creative excellence — something they have never measured.
The First Trial-Master's broken standard held. Return and exceed it — do not try to meet it.
codex: The Laurel-Sky Gate is the Olympian Gate, built on the principle that excellence requires witness. What is unwitnessed does not exist in this Realm — the Gate has made visibility the condition of reality. The first Hollow contact came through corrupted trial remnants: divine athletes who failed their trials and were forgotten, becoming Hollow husks of excellence with all the form and none of the glory.

The Olympian Summit of Olympos is the source Realm; mortal Greece is only the later echo. The Laurel-Sky Gate tests not strength but memorability — whether the deity's excellence is worth recording. The Gate's trial-constructs measure every action against the divine standard, punishing anything below excellence.

The First Trial-Master is a corrupted version of the original Olympian judge, measuring with a broken standard designed to never be met. The deity cannot pass by meeting the standard — only by exceeding it so far that the standard itself breaks. This establishes the Olympian theme: excellence is not compliance. Excellence is transcendence.

intro: Oracle Vapor Bleed. The Oracle's breath has been corrupted — her prophecies now serve the Gate, not the gods. The vapor makes truth into lies.
The Oracle's chamber fills with Gate-vapor. Every prophecy it delivers is true — but the truth is weaponized. The Oracle speaks the deity's doom as if it were wisdom.
The vapor thickens. The Oracle's prophecies become tactical — she tells the enemy what the deity will do before they do it. Fight unpredictably or fight a losing battle.
The Oracle's deepest chamber. The vapor is so thick it replaces air. The deity must fight while breathing weaponized truth — every breath tells you how you will fail.
enemy: Vapor-warped oracles. They speak true prophecies — but the truths are all the deity's failures. Every word weakens conviction.
Hollow vapor-sprites. They carry fragments of the Oracle's corrupted breath. Each fragment is a true prediction of the deity's next move. Fight against your own future.
Gate-prophets. They have consumed the Oracle's vapor and gained her foresight. They counter every move before it happens. Be unpredictable — or be predicted to death.
The Corrupted Oracle. She speaks with the voice of the original prophetess but serves the Gate. Her final prophecy: 'You will lose.' Make her wrong.
mid: The vapor tells truth — but truth is not destiny. The Oracle sees what will happen if you act as you always have. Act as you never have.
The prophecies are tactical. They predict your moves. Break the prediction — do something the Oracle cannot foresee because you have never done it.
The vapor-sprites carry your future. Do not breathe them. Hold your breath. Fight without the air of prophecy. You do not need to know your future to fight for it.
The Corrupted Oracle says you will lose. Make her wrong — not by fighting harder, but by fighting in a way she cannot predict. Her prophecy is true only if you fulfill it.
victory: The vapor clears. The Oracle's prophecies were true — but you broke the timeline by acting outside prediction. The Oracle's first false prophecy is your victory.
The vapor-sprites dissolve. You fought without breathing prophecy. The future is not the air you need — it is the ground you make.
The Gate-prophets fall. They predicted every move you have ever made — but you made moves you have never made. Prediction failed. Excellence prevailed.
The Corrupted Oracle's final prophecy is proven false. 'You will lose' was true only if you accepted it. You refused. The Oracle's chamber is clear.
defeat: Withdraw. The vapor truths weakened your conviction. Return with the knowledge that truth is not destiny.
The prophecies predicted everything. Return with unpredictability — do something you have never done.
The vapor-sprites poisoned your air. Return with held breath — fight without prophecy.
The Oracle's prophecy held. You fulfilled it. Return and refuse — do not accept the future she speaks.
codex: Oracle Vapor Bleed is the corruption of the Olympian Oracle — the prophetic voice of the Summit. The Gate has turned her breath into weaponized truth: every prophecy is accurate, but the accuracy is used against the deity. The Oracle speaks the deity's doom as tactical intelligence, giving enemies foresight of every move. The trial is not to silence the Oracle but to fight unpredictably — to act in ways the prophecy cannot foresee because the deity has never done them.

The Corrupted Oracle serves the Gate, not the Summit. Her prophecies are true — but truth is not destiny. The deity's victory comes from breaking the timeline: acting outside the pattern the Oracle can read. This establishes the Olympian principle that excellence includes the capacity for surprise — the ability to transcend one's own patterns.

The vapor itself is weaponized. Breathing it means inhaling predictions of failure. The deity must fight without the air of prophecy — holding breath, fighting without the comfort of knowing the future. This is the Olympian trial of faith: fight for a future you cannot see.

intro: The Laurel Trial of Blood. The old Olympic trials were tests of excellence. The Gate has turned them into tests of survival. Excellence is no longer enough — endurance is required.
The trial arena shifts. What was once a competition is now a siege. The deity must excel not for a moment but for hours. Sustained excellence.
The trial-constructs have been enhanced. They no longer just measure — they attack. Every measurement is a blade. Every standard is a weapon.
The Blood Trial's final arena. The deity must excel against every enemy the Gate has produced so far — simultaneously. The standard is survival, not victory.
enemy: Enhanced trial-constructs that attack while measuring. Every measurement is a blade — to be below standard is to be cut. To be above standard is to be targeted.
Hollow blood-athletes. They were competitors who died in the trials. They fight with the desperation of the already-dead — there is nothing they will not do.
Trial-constructs measuring sustained excellence. A single moment of mediocrity is a wound. Hours of excellence is the minimum.
Every enemy from the campaign so far, deployed simultaneously. The Blood Trial's standard is not beating them — it is outlasting them.
mid: The constructs attack while measuring. Do not try to meet the standard — exceed it. The blade only cuts those who are average. Be exceptional.
The blood-athletes are desperate — they have nothing to lose. Match their desperation with determination. They died for excellence. Survive for it.
Sustained excellence is harder than momentary brilliance. Pace yourself. The trial does not end when you want it to. It ends when you prove you can last.
Every enemy at once. Do not fight them all — outlast them all. The Blood Trial is not a battle. It is an endurance test. Last.
victory: The Blood Trial is passed. Sustained excellence proven. The constructs could not cut what never dipped below exceptional.
The blood-athletes fall. Their desperation met your determination. They died for excellence — you lived for it. The difference is everything.
Sustained excellence achieved. The trial-constructs could not find a moment of mediocrity to cut. The standard is yours.
Every enemy outlasted. The Blood Trial's arena is clear. The standard was survival — and you are still standing. The Gate's lesson: excellence is not a moment. It is a duration.
defeat: Withdraw. The constructs cut you where you dipped below exceptional. Return with sustained brilliance — no lapses.
The blood-athletes' desperation overwhelmed you. Return with stronger determination.
You ran out of excellence before the trial ran out of tests. Return with endurance.
Every enemy at once was too much to outlast. Return with pacing — do not fight them. Last past them.
codex: The Laurel Trial of Blood transforms the old Olympic trials from competitions into sieges. The Gate has weaponized the concept of measurement: trial-constructs now attack while measuring, and the standard itself is a blade. Sustained excellence — the ability to maintain divine performance over hours, not moments — is the trial's core requirement. This is the Olympian trial of endurance: excellence is not a peak but a plateau.

Hollow blood-athletes are the remains of competitors who died in the trials. They fight with the desperation of the already-dead — nothing to lose, everything to prove. They represent the Gate's weaponization of failure: those who could not achieve excellence in life become enemies of excellence in death.

The Blood Trial's final arena deploys every enemy type simultaneously. The standard is not victory but survival — outlasting every enemy the Gate has produced. This redefines the Olympian understanding of excellence: the best competitor is not the one who wins fastest but the one who is still standing when everything else has fallen.

intro: The Marble Throne Archive. The deepest records of Olympian law. The Gate has sealed them — what lies inside changes the deity's understanding of their own Realm.
The archive reveals that the Olympian trials were not created to test excellence. They were created to prevent it. The Gate built the trials to keep the gods below their potential.
The records show the Gate's manipulation: every Olympian trial was designed to cap divine power. The gods who passed were the ones the Gate deemed safe. The gods who failed were the ones it feared.
The final archive chamber. The Gate's original purpose for the Olympian Realm: a training ground for deities the Gate could control. The truth is a cage — and the cage is the Gate.
enemy: Hollow archive-guardians. They protect the sealed records with the desperation of those who know the truth is more dangerous than the enemy.
Gate-altered trial-constructs. They enforce the original purpose: preventing excellence. They are not measuring the deity — they are suppressing the deity.
Hollow marble-golems. They are made of the same marble as the Olympian deities — the Gate has weaponized divine skin itself. Fight against yourself.
The Archive Warden. A Gate construct built from the original Olympian law. It enforces the cap on divine power. Break it or remain capped.
mid: The archive is sealed with divine marble. The same material that makes Olympian skin makes the door. You must break your own skin to enter.
The trials were cages. The Gate built them to prevent excellence, not test it. Knowing this changes everything — but first, survive the constructs that enforce the cap.
The marble-golems are made of divine skin. Fighting them is fighting yourself. But you are alive — they are not. Life exceeds marble.
The Archive Warden enforces the power cap. It was built to keep gods below their potential. Breaking it means breaking the limit the Gate placed on you. You will never be the same.
victory: The archive opens. The truth is worse than feared: the trials were cages. But knowing the cage is the first step to breaking it.
The suppressing constructs fall. Your excellence was never tested — it was capped. Now the cap is broken. What you do with uncapped power is the real trial.
The marble-golems shatter. You defeated yourself — and won. Life exceeded marble. The archive is open.
The Archive Warden breaks. The power cap shatters. You feel what the Gate was afraid of — and you understand why it built the cage. But understanding is not acceptance.
defeat: Withdraw. You could not break your own marble. Return with the knowledge that the cage was built from your own skin.
The suppressing constructs held. Return with uncapped excellence — the kind the Gate built the trials to prevent.
The marble-golems were too much like you. Return with the difference — you are alive. They are not.
The Archive Warden's cap held. Return with the power the Gate feared — the power it built the trials to prevent.
codex: The Marble Throne Archive reveals the Gate's deepest manipulation of the Olympian Realm: the trials were never tests. They were cages. Every Olympian trial was designed to cap divine power — to keep the gods below their potential. The gods who passed were deemed safe; the gods who failed were the ones the Gate feared. This revelation transforms the Olympian campaign from a trial of excellence to a war of liberation.

The Archive Warden is the Gate construct that enforces the power cap on Olympian deities. Breaking it means breaking the limit the Gate placed on divine potential — an irreversible change. The deity emerges from the archive not just with knowledge but with power the Gate spent millennia suppressing. The question is no longer whether the deity can pass the trial but what the deity will do with uncapped power.

The revelation that the trials were cages recontextualizes every previous chapter. The Blood Trial was not testing endurance — it was burning excess power. The Oracle Vapor was not testing unpredictability — it was suppressing foresight. Every Olympian trial was a mechanism of control disguised as a test of merit. The campaign is now a war against the Gate's original design.

intro: The False Laurel Judge. The Gate's final guardian in the Olympian Realm. It wears a laurel wreath it did not earn and judges with a standard it did not set.
The Judge demands excellence — but its standard is the Gate's standard, not the Summit's. It judges the deity against the cap it imposed. Exceed the cap and the Judge fails.
The False Laurel Judge calls corrupted witnesses — every being who failed the original trials. They testify that the deity's excellence is just another form of the cap. Prove them wrong.
Final trial. The Judge's standard is the cage. The deity's excellence is the key. Exceed the standard so far that the cage itself breaks. The Laurel-Sky Gate's final test is to destroy the test.
enemy: The False Laurel Judge. It wears an unearned laurel and judges with the Gate's standard — the cap on divine power. Its attacks are measurements: anything within the cap is punished.
Corrupted trial-failures as witnesses. They testify that excellence within the cap is just compliance — not real excellence. They are right. Exceed the cap to prove it.
Hollow laurel-guardians. They enforce the Judge's standard. Their attacks intensify as the deity exceeds the cap — they are the Gate's immune response to un-capped power.
The False Laurel Judge in its final form. It has absorbed the power cap and become it. To defeat the Judge is to defeat the limit itself. The deity must be more than the Gate's standard allows.
mid: The Judge judges by the Gate's standard — the cap. Anything within the cap is 'excellent' and therefore 'safe.' Exceed the cap. Be dangerous. The Judge cannot measure what exceeds its standard.
The corrupted witnesses are right — excellence within the cap is compliance. Prove them wrong by exceeding the cap. Real excellence is what the Gate tried to prevent.
The laurel-guardians intensify as you exceed the cap. Good. Let them come — every attack is proof you are beyond the standard. The Gate's immune response is the evidence of your liberation.
The Judge has become the cap. To fight it is to fight the limit itself. Do not try to defeat it — transcend it. Be so excellent that the standard becomes irrelevant.
victory: The False Laurel Judge falls. Its unearned laurel crumbles. The standard it enforced was a cage — and you exceeded it so far that the cage shattered. The Olympian trials are over. The real trial begins.

The corrupted witnesses are disproven. Excellence within the cap was compliance — you exceeded the cap. The witnesses were right about the cap and wrong about you. You are not compliance. You are transcendence.
The laurel-guardians fall. The Gate's immune response to un-capped power was overwhelming — and you overwhelmed it. The immune response is no longer a threat. It is a trophy.

Final trial: the test destroyed by the tested. The Laurel-Sky Gate's cap is broken. The Olympian deity stands un-capped — more powerful than the Gate ever allowed. The campaign is won. The war has changed.
defeat: Withdraw. The Judge's standard held. Return with excellence that exceeds the cap — do not fight within it.
The corrupted witnesses' testimony held. Return with excellence so far beyond the cap that compliance is impossible.
The laurel-guardians overwhelmed your un-capped power. Return with more — the immune response is the proof you are dangerous. Let it come.
The Judge became the cap and you could not exceed it. Return and transcend — do not defeat the standard. Exceed it so far it becomes irrelevant.
codex: The False Laurel Judge is the Gate's final guardian in the Olympian Realm. It wears an unearned laurel wreath and judges with the Gate's standard — the cap on divine power that the trials were built to enforce. The deity's victory is not to meet the standard but to exceed it so far that the standard itself becomes irrelevant. This is the Olympian thesis: real excellence is what the Gate tried to prevent. The trial was the cage. Destroying the trial is the victory.

The defeat of the False Laurel Judge does not close the Laurel-Sky Gate. It breaks the power cap the Gate placed on Olympian deities. The deity emerges un-capped — more powerful than the Gate ever allowed. This changes the war: the Olympian deity is now the most powerful weapon the campaign has produced. But power without wisdom is what the Gate feared. The deity must now prove the Gate wrong not just about the cap but about what uncapped power looks like.

The Olympian campaign's central lesson: excellence is not compliance with a standard. Excellence is the transcendence of standards. The Gate built trials to prevent gods from reaching their potential — the deity's victory is reaching that potential anyway. The laurel is not earned by meeting the standard. It is earned by destroying it.

intro: Elite Laurel-Sky Gate. The trial has learned from your first crossing. The corrupted remnants now measure with Elite standards — higher, sharper, and designed to find your specific weakness.
Elite trial-constructs that score creativity as well as excellence. What was new in the Normal campaign is now expected. Invent again.
Elite laurel-wraiths with evolved bitterness. They do not just hate the forgotten — they hate the remembered. Your previous victory makes you their target.
The Elite First Trial-Master with a self-repairing standard. It no longer breaks when exceeded — it adapts. You must exceed adaptation.
enemy: Elite corrupted remnants with adaptive standards. They learn your excellence in real-time and raise the bar. Stay ahead of the adaptation.
Elite trial-constructs scoring creativity. Your Normal-campaign innovation is now the baseline. Innovate beyond your own innovation.
Elite laurel-wraiths targeting the remembered. Your previous victory is their fuel. They fight with the hatred of those who know you won before.
The self-repairing Trial-Master. Exceeding it makes it adapt. You must exceed adaptation itself — be so creative that the standard cannot keep up.
mid: The adaptive standards learn in real-time. Do not repeat any excellence — every action must be new. The constructs are studying you. Be unstudyable.
Creativity is now scored. Your previous innovation is expected. Innovate beyond innovation — find excellence that is not just new but unprecedented.
The wraiths hate you because you won. Use their hatred — let it fuel your excellence. They fight harder against the remembered. Be more memorable.
The self-repairing standard adapts to every exceedance. Do not try to break it — try to outpace it. The standard cannot adapt to speed of thought.
victory: Elite threshold cleared. The adaptive standards could not keep up with your rate of innovation. The Gate learned that creativity is not a resource to be measured — it is a force to be survived.
Creativity scored and exceeded. You out-innovated your own innovation. The Gate has no baseline for you anymore.
The Elite wraiths fell. Their hatred of the remembered met a memory worth hating — and losing to. Your excellence is now twice witnessed.
The self-repairing standard could not adapt fast enough. You outpaced adaptation itself. The First Trial-Master is gone — and with it, the concept of a standard for you.
defeat: Withdraw. The adaptive standards caught up. Return with faster innovation — be unstudyable.
Creativity scored below expectation. Return with unprecedented excellence — not just new, but never-before-imagined.
The wraiths' hatred overwhelmed you. Return with more memorable excellence — let their hatred fuel you.
The self-repairing standard out-adapted you. Return with speed of thought — the standard cannot adapt to what it cannot predict fast enough.
codex: Elite Laurel-Sky Gate missions test whether the deity's first excellence was reproducible. The Gate has evolved the trial-constructs with adaptive standards that learn in real-time and self-repairing measurements that no longer break when exceeded. The deity must outpace adaptation itself — producing excellence faster than the standard can learn. This establishes that the Olympian Gate's deepest lesson is not just creativity but the rate of creativity: innovation speed as a form of power.

intro: Elite Oracle Vapor. The Oracle's breath now carries not just prophecies but counter-prophecies — predictions of actions the deity has not yet considered. The vapor fights not what you will do but what you could do.
Elite vapor-sprites that carry not just predictions but probabilities. Every possible future is a weapon. The deity must fight against every version of themselves.
Elite Gate-prophets with enhanced foresight. They predict not just the deity's moves but the deity's thoughts. Unpredictability is no longer enough — unthinkability is required.
The Elite Corrupted Oracle. She has consumed every prophecy ever spoken and can now predict any action that has been thought. The deity must act without thought — pure instinct.
enemy: Counter-prophecy vapor. It predicts not what you will do but what you could do. Every option is a weapon. You must find the option the vapor cannot predict — the impossible one.
Probability-sprites. They carry every possible future. Fighting them means fighting every version of yourself that could exist. Be the version they cannot carry.
Thought-reading prophets. They predict your moves before you think them. Unpredictability is not enough — you must be unthinking. Pure instinct.
The Elite Oracle has consumed all prophecy. She can predict any action that has been thought. Act without thought — instinct that has never been a thought before.
mid: Counter-prophecies predict every option. Find the impossible option — the one that cannot be predicted because it should not work. Make it work.
Probability-sprites carry every possible you. Do not fight any version — be a version that is impossible. The impossible has no probability.
Thought-reading prophets see your mind. Stop thinking. Act on the body's wisdom — the nerves that fire before the brain decides. Instinct is faster than thought.
The Oracle consumed all prophecy. Act without thought — before the thought exists, it cannot be prophesied. The body knows. Let the body act.
victory: The counter-prophecies failed. You found the impossible option — the one that should not work — and made it work. The vapor cannot predict the impossible.
Probability-sprites dissolved. You became a version of yourself that was impossible — no probability, no prediction. The vapor cannot carry what cannot exist.
The thought-reading prophets fell. Instinct was faster than thought — the body acted before the mind decided. The prophets could not predict what had not been thought.
The Elite Oracle is silenced. She consumed all prophecy but could not prophesy the unthought. Pure instinct — the body's wisdom — defeated the mind of the Oracle. The chamber is clear.
defeat: Withdraw. The counter-prophecies predicted every option. Return with the impossible — the option that should not work.
Probability-sprites overwhelmed you with every version. Return with the impossible version — no probability.
The prophets read your thoughts. Return with instinct — act before thinking.
The Oracle prophesied your every action. Return with the unthought — pure body wisdom.
codex: Elite Oracle Vapor missions escalate the trial from unpredictability to unthinkability. The Oracle's breath now carries counter-prophecies that predict every possible action, and thought-reading prophets that predict actions before they are thought. The deity must act on pure instinct — the body's wisdom that fires before the brain decides. Instinct cannot be prophesied because it has not been thought. This is the Elite Olympian trial: the mind is the enemy. Only the body can win.

intro: Elite Blood Trial. The arena now tests not just sustained excellence but infinite excellence. The trial does not end — it escalates. Last forever or fall.
Elite enhanced trial-constructs that measure and attack with increasing intensity. The longer the trial lasts, the sharper the measurements and the heavier the attacks.
Elite blood-athletes with the power of the already-dead and the endurance of the Hollow. They do not tire. They do not stop. Neither can you.
The Elite final arena: every enemy from Normal AND Elite campaigns deployed simultaneously. The standard is no longer survival — it is eternity.
enemy: Escalating trial-constructs. The measurements sharpen and the attacks intensify with every passing minute. Excellence must grow infinitely or be cut.
Elite blood-athletes with Hollow endurance. They do not tire — they are already dead. Outlast the dead with living will.
Elite sustained-excellence constructs that measure not hours but days. The trial has no time limit — only a will limit. Your will vs the Gate's patience.
Every enemy from both campaigns. The standard is eternity — outlast everything the Gate has ever produced. The trial ends when you stop. Do not stop.
mid: The trial escalates infinitely. Do not try to keep up — try to accelerate. Your excellence must grow faster than the trial's intensity.
The dead do not tire. But they also do not grow. You grow. Let the trial sharpen you — every cut makes you faster. Turn the trial's escalation into your own.
The trial has no time limit — only a will limit. The Gate is patient. You must be more patient. Out-wait the infinite. The trial cannot last forever — but your will can.
Every enemy at once, forever. Do not fight them. Do not outlast them. Outgrow them. Every moment, become more excellent than the last. The enemies are fixed. You are not.
victory: The escalating trial could not keep up with your accelerating excellence. The Gate's infinite intensity met a will that grows faster than infinity. The trial broke — not from violence, but from being outpaced.
The dead fell to the living. Hollow endurance met living growth. The dead do not tire — but they also do not change. You changed every moment. They could not keep up with what you became.
The will limit was reached — but it was the Gate's will that broke, not yours. The trial's patience was finite. Your will was not. The standard is yours.
Every enemy outgrown. The trial asked for eternity and you provided it — not by lasting but by growing. The enemies were fixed. You were infinite. The Blood Trial is complete.
defeat: Withdraw. The escalation outpaced you. Return with accelerating excellence — grow faster than the trial sharpens.
The dead out-endured you. Return with living growth — change every moment or the dead will outlast the living.
The Gate's patience outlasted your will. Return with more — the will limit is the only limit. Break it.
Every enemy was too much to outgrow. Return with infinite growth — become more excellent every moment.
codex: Elite Blood Trial missions test not just sustained excellence but infinite escalation. The trial has no end — it intensifies forever. The deity's victory is not in lasting but in growing: outpacing the trial's infinite intensity with accelerating excellence. This reveals the Elite Olympian principle: excellence is not a state but a rate. The god who grows faster than the trial sharpens is the god who wins. Fixed power is finite. Growing power is infinite.

intro: Elite Marble Throne Archive. The Gate has sealed the deepest records behind a double cap — not just preventing power but erasing the memory of power. The deity must find what was erased.
Elite suppressing constructs that enforce not just the power cap but the memory cap. They make the deity forget their own potential. Fight while forgetting what you are.
Elite marble-golems made of divine skin and divine memory. They carry the deity's capped power and capped memories. Fight your forgotten self.
The Elite Archive Warden enforces a double cap — power and memory. Breaking it means remembering what you are and becoming what you were. The transformation is irreversible.
enemy: Memory-capping constructs. They do not just suppress power — they erase the knowledge of power. You must fight while forgetting you can fight. Instinct is the only weapon that survives memory loss.
Suppressing constructs with double enforcement: power cap and memory cap. They make you weaker and make you forget you were ever strong. Fight on instinct — it is all they leave you.
Divine-skin golems carrying your capped power and forgotten memories. They are what the Gate took from you — walking, fighting, attacking. Fight the version of yourself the Gate created.
The Elite Warden with double cap enforcement. It keeps you below your power and below your memory. Breaking it means double liberation: remembering and becoming. The Gate fears both.
mid: You are forgetting. The constructs are erasing your knowledge of your own power. Do not try to remember — act. The body remembers what the mind forgets. Instinct carries forgotten power.
Double cap: power and memory. You cannot fight with what you cannot remember. But instinct does not need memory. Let the body fight — it remembers everything the mind has lost.
The golems carry what was taken. Do not fight them — reclaim them. Your capped power is in their fists. Your forgotten memories are in their eyes. Take them back.
The Warden caps power and memory. Breaking one is not enough — break both. Remember and become simultaneously. The double liberation is the only escape from the double cap.
victory: The memory cap breaks. You remember what you are — and the power cap shatters with it. You cannot cap power when the capped one remembers they are powerful. Double liberation achieved.
Instinct carried what memory lost. The body fought the entire battle — and won. When the mind returned, it found a victory it did not plan. The body is the better warrior.
The golems are reclaimed. Your capped power and forgotten memories return. You are whole — for the first time since the Gate capped you. The archive is open. The truth is yours.
The Elite Warden's double cap shatters. You remember and become simultaneously. The Gate's deepest cage — the one that made you forget you were caged — is broken. You are what you were meant to be.
defeat: Withdraw. You forgot too much. Return with instinct — the body remembers what the mind loses.
The double cap was too strong. Return with double liberation — remember and become at once.
The golems took too much. Return and reclaim — your power and memory are in their fists and eyes.
The Elite Warden's double cap held. Return with the double break — remembering and becoming are one act.
codex: Elite Marble Throne Archive missions reveal the Gate's deepest cage: the memory cap. Not only did the Gate cap Olympian power — it erased the knowledge that power was ever capped. The deity must fight while forgetting what they are, relying on instinct to carry what memory cannot. Breaking the double cap means double liberation: remembering what was taken and becoming what was lost. The Gate's deepest fear is not uncapped power — it is uncapped memory. A god who remembers they were caged is a god who will never be caged again.

intro: Elite False Laurel Judge. It now carries not just the cap but the memory cap — it judges with a standard the deity has forgotten. You must exceed a standard you cannot remember.
The Elite Judge calls not just corrupted witnesses but erased witnesses — beings whose existence the Gate has deleted. They testify from non-existence. Disprove non-existence.
The Elite Judge's standard is now the double cap: power and memory. Exceed both. Be more than the cap allows and more than the cap remembers. Double transcendence.

Final Elite trial. The Judge carries every cap the Gate ever imposed. The deity must exceed every limit simultaneously — power, memory, and existence itself. The standard is everything. The deity must be more.
enemy: The Elite Judge with the memory cap standard. It judges by a limit the deity has forgotten. Exceed a standard you cannot remember — trust instinct. Instinct exceeds any remembered cap.
Erased witnesses from non-existence. They testify that the deity's excellence is a Gate-authorized program — permitted because it is contained. Disprove containment by exceeding every boundary.
Double-cap Judge: power and memory. It enforces both limits simultaneously. Exceed both — be more powerful than the cap and more aware than the memory erasure. Double transcendence.
